title: Heatcheck Containment and Executive Escalation Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical, execution-oriented playbook for early-warning ("heatcheck") customer signals ahead of renewals. Focus: rapid containment, targeted mitigation plays, and a clean executive escalation path when escalations are required. Designed for CS reps, AMs, and CS leadership to use in the 0–90 day window before a renewal decision.

Scope and intent:
- Covers identification of risk signals, scoring, immediate containment actions (first 48 hours), medium-term mitigation (2–30 days), and formal exec escalation triggers and templates.
- Emphasis on measurable commitments, tight timelines, and who-owns-what. Not a policy doc; this is an operational runbook to be used in live saves.

Definitions (quick):
- Heatcheck: an observed signal (usage drop, NPS drop, exec disengagement) that moves an account from green to amber.
- Containment: short-term actions to stop further deterioration (communication cadence, targeted triage).
- Save play: a bundled mitigation sequence (technical fix + adoption push + commercial offer) executed to recover confidence.

Common signals (examples):
- Usage down > 25% week-over-week for core feature set.
- QBR shows negative ROI narrative or top three priorities misaligned.
- Critical bug or repeated incidents > 2 in last 30 days.
- Exec sponsor changes or prolonged silence (> 21 days between replies).
- Inbound churn signals: procurement delays, legal stalls, competitor PoC.

Signal scoring matrix (simple):
(Assign 0–3 points each)
- Usage impact: 0 none /1 minor /2 material /3 core-blocker
- Financial exposure: 0 <$5k /1 $5–25k /2 $25–100k /3 >$100k ARR at stake
- Exec engagement: 0 healthy /1 fading /2 absent /3 sponsor left
- Product incidents: 0 none /1 low /2 recurring /3 severity-critical
Total: 0–12. Triage bands: 0–3 green, 4–6 amber, 7–9 red, 10–12 firebreak (immediate exec).

Immediate containment (first 48 hours) — play checklist:
1) Rapid internal huddle (30 min) — attendees: AM/CS rep, Solutions engineer, On-call SRE (if incident), Customer Success Manager lead.
2) Snapshot packet (30 min) — create a one-pager for the customer: current usage trends, open incidents, timeline of outreach, proposed immediate next steps. Attach last 90 days of telemetry.
3) Customer outreach: 24-hour window to acknowledge and commit to a 72-hour recovery plan if incident-related, or schedule a 48-hour strategy sync if non-incident. Use the acknowledgement template below.
4) Temporary mitigations: enable short-term throttles, add pre-baked support runbooks, or rotate SLA on-call to the account depending on severity.
5) Escalation determination: if score >= 7, prepare exec escalation (see triggers).

Escalation triggers (send to CS Director/Head of CS + CRO):
- Total score >= 10 (firebreak).
- Customer expresses intent to not renew or to evaluate competitors.
- Legal or finance threatens contract non-renewal within 60 days.
- Any severity-critical incident impacting production SLAs for > 4 hours.

Executive escalation template (email + Slack sequence):
Subject: [Escalation] Account: <Account> — Heatcheck score <n> — Immediate ask
Slack (to #cs-escalations + @cs-director): "Escalation: <Account> — Score <n>. Key facts: usage down X%, incidents Y, exec silence Z days. Immediate ask: decision on one-time concession / deployment of senior SE / trial of Dedicated capacity. Packet: <link to snapshot>"
Email body (one paragraph):
- TL;DR: We have a high-severity retention risk at <Account>. Timeline of key signals and interventions to date. Customer stance: <brief>. Proposed mitigation: <3-line play>. Ask from leadership: <decision, resource, approval>. Appendments: telemetry + engagement log.

Mitigation play catalog (pick and adapt) — short descriptions:
1) Technical Hotfix + Priority SR: Engage SRE/SE, provide a 7-day dedicated incident bridge, waive support fees for the recovery window.
2) Adoption Blitz: Run a 3-session workshop series focused on the account's top 3 use cases (deliverable: adoption playbook and success checklist).
3) ROI Reconnect: Finance-backed ROI re-derivation with customer execs; show delta of current approach vs target.
4) Commercial Makegood: Offer a one-time credit or discount tied to explicit operational milestones (1% credit per missed SLA, capped). Keep approvals pre-authorized for small bands (see commercial guardrails).
5) Pilot of Dedicated/Private capacity: fast-track a 30-day pilot of Dedicated pool for performance-sensitive customers (requires IR for infra capacity).
6) Executive-to-Executive Introductions: short 15-min slates between Redwood exec + customer exec to reestablish sponsorship.

Commercial guardrails (for CS reps):
- Tier A accounts (> $250k ARR): escalations to CRO for credits/concessions > 3% ARR equivalent.
- Tier B accounts ($50–250k): CS Director approval for concessions up to 3%.
- Tier C (< $50k): CS Manager can approve credits up to $2,500.
All credits must be tied to measurable commitments and documented in Salesforce with a 90-day follow-up plan.

QBR talking points for at-risk accounts (script bullets):
- Reframe: "We want to ensure Redwood is delivering X value; here are the metrics we tracked."
- Show change: usage trends, feature adoption, incidents, business impact.
- Listen: ask 3 open questions about customer's top priorities and blockers.
- Propose: specific next three actions (who, what, when).
- Commit: timeline for mitigation and date for check-in (max 14 days).

Customer-facing 30/60/90 commitment timeline (sample):
- Day 0–3: Acknowledge + containment + schedule exec sync if needed.
- Day 4–14: Execute technical triage and adoption plays. Provide weekly progress notes.
- Day 15–30: Deliver commercial remediation (if any) and measure adoption lift.
- Day 31–90: Monitor metrics, agree on renewal readiness criteria, and finalize QBR narrative.

Roles and responsibilities (quick roster):
- CS Rep / AM: owner of customer communication and play coordination.
- Solutions Engineer: technical remediation and runbooks.
- SRE: incidents & performance investigations.
- CS Manager / Director: approval of mid-size concessions and interface with leadership.
- Finance/Sales Ops: executes contract adjustments.
- Legal: supports any contract amendments.

Checklist templates (use copy-paste in CRM):
- Initial contact logged (Y/N)
- Snapshot packet uploaded (link)
- 48-hour plan agreed (date)
- Technical SR created (id)
- Commercial offer documented (terms)
- Executive escalation sent (when)

After-action & learning:
- Capture root cause and timeline in Confluence within 7 days of mitigation close.
- Run a 30-min blameless retrospective with involved stakeholders to extract one process improvement and one product ask.
- Feed product asks into the product intake board with priority and owner.

Templates (appendix snippets):
- Acknowledgement email (24h): "Thanks for the flag. We’re investigating — immediate steps include X, Y. We will confirm a 72-hour plan by <date>."
- Executive intro request (short): "<Customer Exec> — quick request: can you join a 15-min call with our CRO to align on roadmap alignment and ensure we’re meeting your priorities?"

Quick notes on evidence & audit trail:
- Always attach telemetry screenshots (timestamps) and call notes to the account in Salesforce.
- Tag the case with "heatcheck" and include the score.
- Use the Slack escalation channel and thread so leadership decisions and approvals are visible.

Playbook maintenance and ownership:
- This playbook maintained by CS Operations (owner: Sofia Martinez).
- Quarterly review cadence; update sheet with new mitigation plays, guardrail thresholds, and approved credit bands.

Appendix: example of a completed snapshot packet (collapsed into bullets for Drive doc):
- Executive summary: 2 lines.
- Key metrics: ARR at risk, usage delta, incident count.
- Engagement log: last 90 days (dates + short notes).
- Proposed 14-day plan: owners + deliverables.
- Asks for leadership: 2 decisions needed.

End of document.

Notes to self (working):
- Add link to the standard support waiver form.
- Confirm Dedicated capacity pilot approval workflow with Infra (Amit).
- Draft SFDC checkbox automation to tag heatcheck accounts.
